beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: These two quadrilaterals look alike. Could the orange one be the blue one, just moved?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A transformed figure is called its image. We will measure what a slide, a flip, or a turn cannot change.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: First, measure a sloping side. From *A*, zero, zero, to *B*, four, two: four across and two up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Those steps are perpendicular. The straight distance is the hypotenuse, not the sum of the steps.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: By the Pythagorean theorem, the length squared is four squared plus two squared: twenty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So the length is the square root of twenty, or two square roots of five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Attach the measurements to the figure: two side lengths and a ninety degree angle. The arrow marks identify parallel sides.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slope is the change in height divided by the change across. Both parallel sides have slope one half.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A translation is a slide. Move every point two left and one down.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: New coordinates. The same lengths, the same angle, and parallel sides.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A reflection flips the figure across a line. Here, the vertical axis is the mirror.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Flip it. Each corner lands equally far on the other side. The measurements travel with it.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Follow the corners in alphabetical order. They go around the opposite way. Reflection reverses that order, but keeps the angles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A rotation is a turn around a fixed point. Turn ninety degrees counterclockwise around the origin.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The slopes change together, from negative one half to two. The sides stay parallel to each other.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That is rigid motion: every distance and every angle is preserved. Nothing stretches or bends.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Check the turned figure from its coordinates. For the long side, the changes are negative two across and negative four up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Square both changes. Four plus sixteen is twenty, exactly the original length squared.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For slope, divide the change in height by the change across. Negative four over negative two is two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From *D*, negative one, three, to *C*, negative two, one, the slope is also two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Distinct lines with equal slopes are parallel.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two vertical lines are parallel too, although their slopes are undefined.

do.text: Vertical lines: both go straight up

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A straight line stays straight, too. Turn these three points together.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: After the turn, both consecutive segments have slope negative one. Because they share the middle point, all three points lie on one line.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here is a four by three rectangle. Predict the corner after a ninety degree turn.

do.text: The turn is not added to the angle

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The whole corner turns. Its opening does not grow.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: To verify that right angle by measuring, compare the three sides of this triangle: three, four, five.

do.text: Measure to verify the right angle

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Sixteen plus nine equals twenty-five. By the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, the angle opposite the longest side is ninety degrees.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For a claims question, select every true statement: the side is four; the corner is ninety degrees; opposite sides stay parallel.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Area stays the same too: twelve square units.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A turn preserves the order of the corners. A reflection reverses it.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: To choose a possible image, match corresponding corners in order: *A* with *P*, *B* with *Q*, and so on.

do.text: Which graph could be the image?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For this parallelogram, the side lengths are seven and five. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Also check a diagonal, which joins opposite corners. From *B* to *D*, go three left and three up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Its length squared is nine plus nine: eighteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Graph one: this side measures eight, but its matching side measured seven. Reject it.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Graph two: the bottom side has slope zero. The top side rises one unit over seven. Those sides are not parallel. Reject it.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Graph three is more deceptive. Its sides are seven and five, and opposite sides are parallel. Is that enough?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Measure the diagonal. From *Q* to *S*, go four left and four up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Its length squared is thirty-two, not eighteen. The sides match, but the figure has opened to a different angle.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Different squares mean different lengths. One changed distance proves this was not a rigid motion.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Watch why matching sides are not enough. Start with the original shape, and keep all four side lengths fixed.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Open the angle. The diagonal grows, even though no side stretches. This bends the figure; it is not a rigid motion.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Graph four keeps all four side lengths and both diagonals in the matching order. It can be the image.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here is the original. Reflect it across the horizontal axis. Every corner lands exactly on its partner.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A mirror image qualifies. The letters run the other way, but no measurement changed.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to our opening pair. The blue side went four across and two up. The orange side goes five across and two up.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Twenty and twenty-nine. That one changed length is enough: this pair cannot be related by a rigid motion.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A rigid motion changes where a figure is, while preserving every distance and angle. When in doubt, measure.
